item.title: High-frequency data show improving trend in Chinese economy in October
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
High-frequency data show improving trend in Chinese economy in October BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese economy maintained its steady and improving trend in October, with new growth drivers gaining momentum, official high-frequency data on consumption, trade and investment showed Friday. Big data on offline consumption showed that consumption-related payments increased 2.6 percent year on year in October, according to the State Information Center under the National Development and Reform Commission. Benefits from various consumption-boosting policies continued to materialize, supporting the consumer market's steady growth, according to Geng Dewei, an associate researcher at the center's big data development department. "Service consumption in clothing, food, housing, transportation and tourism has improved simultaneously, and diverse consumption scenarios have been continuously activated," Geng said. The data also showed that the departure deadweight tonnage of cargo ships at major Chinese ports increased 59.1 percent year on year in October, with the growth rate 5.9 percentage points higher than that in September. On the investment front, the contract value of winning bids for new infrastructure projects related to computing power and data increased 45.4 percent year on year, while capital investment in frontier fields such as artificial intelligence and humanoid robots soared 307.4 percent. Geng said the effects of policies to stabilize investment are gradually emerging, with allocated funds being translated into physical progress and the investment structure being optimized. A State Council executive meeting held last week urged faster progress on the construction and implementation of major projects and the country's "six networks" of infrastructure, covering water, power, computing, communications, urban underground pipelines and logistics networks. It called for strengthening confidence and stepping up policy implementation to ensure China meets its major economic and social development targets for the year. China has targeted 2026 growth at 4.5 to 5 percent and will strive for even better results in practice. China's gross domestic product grew 4.5 percent year on year in the third quarter of 2026, higher than the second quarter's reading of 4.3 percent. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China's 3rd APEC hosting comes amid push for opening-up's next frontier, says APEC secretariat chief
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
China's 3rd APEC hosting comes amid push for opening-up's next frontier, says APEC secretariat chief This photo taken on Nov. 11, 2026 shows an exterior view of the media center for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Mao Siqian) SINGAPORE, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Eduardo Pedrosa, executive director of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Secretariat, said China's further opening-up, including in areas such as the digital economy and artificial intelligence (AI), would create new opportunities for deeper cooperation across the Asia-Pacific and joint efforts to address technological change. "China has been a great leader in this opening-up process," Pedrosa told Xinhua ahead of the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting to be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19. He recalled that China joined APEC in 1991, as its reform and opening-up drive was gaining momentum. It hosted APEC for the first time in 2001, and again in 2014, when connectivity was one of the key priorities. An aerial drone photo taken on Oct. 20, 2026 shows a cargo ship sailing toward Yantian Port in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua) China's third time hosting APEC in 2026 comes as the country moves toward "the next frontier of opening-up," he said. "This includes the digital economy and AI," he said. "How do we come together in that space to cooperate on how to move forward in an innovative way, but still safeguard our citizens? That involves not just cooperating with a set number, but all members of our region and globally as well." China has identified openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priority areas for this year's APEC agenda. More than 300 meetings and events have been held around these priorities, with substantial progress made, Pedrosa said. On openness, APEC has focused on issues including free trade, services trade and supply chain resilience, he said. In May, APEC ministers responsible for trade met in Suzhou and issued a joint statement outlining a consensus on how to move forward on trade policy issues. APEC subsequently held a series of policy dialogues on trade-related issues, including trade and e-commerce, and trade and labor, Pedrosa said. Pedrosa said the progress on trade also demonstrated APEC's ability to "reach consensus on sometimes very difficult issues." "Trade is a very difficult set of issues at this time, but APEC trade ministers were able to come together, agree on a joint statement, and even plot a way forward on how APEC will address services trade, with a particular focus on innovation," he said. On innovation, the digital economy and AI have been key topics, Pedrosa said. Discussions have covered the use of AI in agriculture, energy and education, as well as financing for digital infrastructure and workforce development. One notable aspect, Pedrosa said, is that "these issues aren't limited to any one agency, but they are relevant across all different types of agencies." This reflects one of APEC's important roles: bringing together policymakers and a wide range of stakeholders from across the region. On cooperation, Pedrosa identified inclusive development as one of this year's key achievements. APEC has explored ways to build more inclusive economies and enable women to participate more fully in economic activity. Economies have also discussed cooperation on energy and support for small and medium-sized enterprises. An aerial drone photo taken on Oct. 10, 2026 shows a view of Huanggang Port in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) Pedrosa said he was looking forward to the leaders' meeting in Shenzhen. "One of the reasons why we're having the leaders' meeting in Shenzhen is because it's a center of innovation for China, but also more globally, how the research and innovation work in Shenzhen can benefit the entire region and the rest of the world as well," he said. Pedrosa said he hoped economies would have candid discussions on AI and sustainable growth, as well as pressing issues such as rising energy prices, inflation and fiscal policy, and explore opportunities for cooperation. APEC economies collectively account for more than 60 percent of global GDP and around 40 percent of the world's population, Pedrosa noted, adding that "we have that critical mass to work together and find ways of dealing with the volatility and uncertainty." item.title: APEC Primer in Four Words | Community: What APEC is and how it works
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
APEC Primer in Four Words | Community: What APEC is and how it works This photo shows a flower decoration themed on the 2026 APEC "China Year," in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) APEC Primer in Four Words: The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18 and 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together." This four-part series unpacks four key words from that theme, one each day, to explain what APEC is and what the 2026 host year is about. The first of those words is "community," because it answers the most basic question: what kind of group is APEC? Before asking what it means to build a community across a region of vastly different economies, cultures and levels of development, it helps to understand how APEC itself works. A forum, not a treaty APEC was established in 1989 by 12 economies and has since grown to 21. It runs on non-binding commitments, open dialogue and equal respect for the views of all participants. Unlike the World Trade Organization, it places no treaty obligations on its members. Decisions are reached by consensus, and every economy has an equal say. This approach lets economies with different systems, development levels and priorities work together without being bound to commitments they haven't chosen to make. Why "economies" APEC calls its participants "member economies," not "countries." The forum explains that its work centers on trade and economic issues, with members engaging one another as economic entities. The 21 member economies range from Australia, Canada and Chile to Japan, Mexico and Vietnam, and include China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. China joined in 1991. A region of scale Together, APEC's member economies are home to about 36 percent of the world's population. They accounted for more than 61 percent of global real GDP in 2025 and about 46 percent of global trade in goods and commercial services in 2024. The member economies are at very different stages of development, from some of the world's largest economies to much smaller ones. That diversity helps explain why the forum's work has centered on practical goals: reducing barriers to trade and investment, and encouraging economic and technical cooperation. How it works Policy direction comes from the leaders of the 21 economies, backed by recommendations from ministers and senior officials. The APEC Secretariat, based in Singapore, supports the work. The business community also has a voice. The APEC Business Advisory Council (ABAC) brings together up to three business representatives from each economy to advise officials and leaders, while the annual APEC CEO Summit provides another platform for business engagement. The host role rotates among members each year, and each host proposes a theme and priorities to guide the year's work. China as host China will host the leaders' meeting for the third time in 2026, following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. This year's theme is "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," with openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priorities. If APEC is already a community of 21 economies, what does it mean to build one that prospers together? That is the question for the next piece in this series: Prosper. item.title: Explainer: How the CPC turns clean governance into momentum for capable officials
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Explainer: How the CPC turns clean governance into momentum for capable officials BEIJING, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- In persevering with full and rigorous self-governance, the Communist Party of China (CPC) highlighted efforts to stimulate Party members' and officials' enthusiasm in tackling challenges. How will the CPC deliver on this commitment? At the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee in October, the CPC leadership sent the signal -- equally important to full and rigorous self-governance is how to encourage Party members and officials to better fulfill their duties, take on new challenges and tackle them. The focus of efforts has been set on creating a clean and enabling political environment. But the drive to stimulate Party members' and officials' enthusiasm doesn't stop here. In an enabling political environment, the next thing they need to better serve the people is competence. Currently, the world is undergoing changes unseen in a century, and China is at a critical moment when the foundation for basically realizing socialist modernization needs to be consolidated and all-out efforts should be made to advance the cause. It is more imperative than ever before to improve the competence of officials. Officials need to develop their abilities to advance high-quality development, serve the people, forestall and defuse risks, and apply law-based thinking and approaches in their work. For this purpose, they are encouraged to work at the primary level, keep abreast of new technologies, new industries and new business models, and learn the latest knowledge and expertise required for the fulfillment of duties. The composition of the CPC membership has changed, with officials born after China's reform and opening-up in 1978 taking up an increasingly large share. The healthy career growth of those officials has been highlighted on the agenda of the CPC's full and rigorous self-governance. The CPC creates opportunities for them to build up their skills and abilities in practice, whether on the front line of reform, development and stability endeavors, in major tasks, or in challenging but key positions. Targeted training programs revolving around social and economic development goals during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) have been planned to help young officials close the knowledge gap and shore up their weaknesses in fulfilling duties. The CPC also pledged to unequivocally support and speak up for those who assume responsibility and do solid work, particularly when they encounter setbacks or criticisms because of their bold and proactive moves in performing duties, or when they suffer from injustice because of misunderstanding or false accusations. The original aspiration and mission of the CPC are to seek happiness for the Chinese people, and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. The CPC understands that the political ideal of serving the people and good governance cannot be achieved if pursuing power for power's sake or personal benefits becomes the ultimate goal of governance. That's why the CPC has been taking a tough stance against corruption particularly since 2012, and why it places such great importance on building a clean political environment and a contingent of capable officials. Governing the Party with strict discipline, the CPC is protecting the level playing field and stimulating positive energy for shouldering responsibilities. In this sense, such a Party self-governance endeavor bolsters economic and social development, and ultimately the wellbeing of the people. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. China-Africa photo exhibition deepens friendship, cultural ties Guests visit the China-Africa Impressions Photography Exhibition in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, Nov. 12, 2026. China-Africa Impressions Photography Exhibition opened Thursday here showcasing cultural ties, people-to-people exchanges and time-honored friendship between China and Africa. Held at the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), the photography exhibition featured 64 photographs, which were selected from 283 entries submitted by 151 photographers of 26 nationalities. (Xinhua/Geng Xinning) ADDIS ABABA, Nov. 12 (Xinhua) -- China-Africa Impressions Photography Exhibition opened Thursday in Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, showcasing cultural ties, people-to-people exchanges and time-honored friendship between China and Africa. Held at the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), the photography exhibition featured 64 photographs, which were selected from 283 entries submitted by 151 photographers of 26 nationalities. The photographs were captured in more than 30 African countries and China. 24 of them won awards for uniquely depicting the diversity of China and Africa, demonstrating their development, achievements, rich cultural heritage, wildlife and landscapes. Opening the exhibition, Jiang Feng, head of the Chinese Mission to the African Union, said the photography exhibition is a vivid example of China-Africa joint efforts to implement the Global Civilization Initiative that calls for respect for the diversity of civilizations, stronger international people-to-people exchanges, and inclusive coexistence and mutual learning. "The exhibition provides an opportunity to further deepen mutual understanding and friendship between the peoples of China and Africa, enable exchanges among civilizations to transcend barriers, and bring our peoples closer across mountains and seas, thus laying a stronger and more enduring foundation of public support for China-Africa friendship," Jiang said. Noting that the China-Africa friendship has a long history and has grown stronger over time, Jiang hopes that the exhibition will open new opportunities to enhance mutual understanding between the peoples of China and Africa, deepen their cultural exchanges and help build an all-weather China-Africa community with a shared future. Mama Keita, deputy executive secretary for programme support at the UNECA, said the photographs showcase everyday moments, bringing together places, cultures and perspectives in a shared visual dialogue, honoring both distinctiveness and common humanity. "I hope these photographs will inspire conversation, broaden our perspectives and encourage us to see our diverse cultures, experiences and heritage with fresh eyes while discovering the common ground that connects China and Africa," she said. The event, co-organized by the Chinese Mission to the African Union and the UNECA, attracted nearly 200 guests. It also came as the two sides celebrate the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges. "As we celebrate the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges, we are reminded that connections between countries are built not only through meetings and agreements, but also through people, curiosity, shared experiences, cultural exchanges and the stories we tell one another," Wubshet Tolosa, representative of award-winning photographers, said during the event. item.title: Jordanian entrepreneur builds thriving business, finds a home in E China's Yiwu
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Jordanian entrepreneur builds thriving business, finds a home in E China's Yiwu Beyti Restaurant in Yiwu, east China's Zhejiang province, is packed with patrons. (Photo/Lyu Bin) Beyti Restaurant on Chouzhou North Road in Yiwu, east China's Zhejiang province, draws a lively crowd of patrons as the aroma of grilled meat wafts from the kitchen. Spotting a regular customer walking in, restaurant owner Mohanad Shalabi steps forward to offer a warm handshake and an embrace, just like welcoming a family member home. Shalabi has been living in China for 26 years. In 2002, he and his wife moved to Yiwu and opened an Arabic restaurant named "Ward," meaning "Flower" in Arabic. Since then, the restaurant, offering culinary delights and a touch of homesickness, has flourished here. Shalabi has not only achieved his entrepreneurial dream, but also found a true sense of belonging in China. Originally from Jordan, Shalabi left his hometown at the age of 17 to make a living, traveling to the Netherlands and Thailand along the way. In 2000, he arrived in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong province, where he worked in an Arabic restaurant run by his uncle, learning how to cook while gaining management experience. "Back then, the seed of entrepreneurship was already planted in my heart," Shalabi recalled. "China's vast market offered boundless opportunities, and I believed my career would succeed here," he said. Later, he married Liu Fang, a woman from east China's Anhui province who worked as an interpreter at the restaurant, making him even more determined to make China his home. Mohanad Shalabi (right) talks with an employee in his restaurant in Yiwu, east China's Zhejiang province. (People's Daily/Liu Junguo) In 2002, through a friend originally from the Middle East, Shalabi learned about Yiwu, a vast market for small commodities where many foreign merchants went to source goods. "My friend told me it was hard to find an authentic Arabic restaurant in Yiwu and suggested I go take a look," Shalabi recalled. He realized the opportunity was right there. At that time, Yiwu, dubbed "the world's capital of small commodities," was in the middle of a crucial period of transformation and upgrading, looking very different from the bustling hub it is today. Yet, the city's hospitality and inclusiveness quickly convinced Shalabi to stay. "Not knowing anyone or the area, I worried that the landlord might raise the rent on us when we were looking for a place. Instead, upon hearing that we were a young couple starting a business, the landlord immediately offered a fair price, helped us move our belongings, and introduced us to the neighborhood," Shalabi recalled. "The good public security also gave us peace of mind. No matter how late we went out, it was completely safe. On top of that, Yiwu's foreign trade was already beginning to gain momentum, offering great market opportunities," said Shalabi. Riding the tailwind of China's accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO), the people of Yiwu stood at the forefront of the reform and opening-up. Merchants from an increasing number of countries flocked to the city in search of business opportunities. Shalabi's original goal was to make sure foreign merchants in Yiwu could enjoy a taste of home. Shalabi opened his first restaurant on Chouzhou North Road, an area frequented by foreign merchants. He named it "Ward" to symbolize flowers of happiness and peace. To his surprise, the small restaurant quickly became a favorite among foreign traders in Yiwu. Bag exhibits attract foreign merchants for viewing and procurement in District 2 of the Yiwu International Trade Market in Yiwu, east China's Zhejiang province. (Photo/Hu Xiaofei) Gradually, foreign merchants began using the restaurant for much more than just dining. Some waited for clients here, while others negotiated deals. Between bowls of chickpea soup and grilled meat, sample catalogs and price sheets often lay spread across the table. "It was a restaurant, but it was more like an open and accessible venue for business negotiations. Many foreign merchants didn't speak Chinese, so my wife, my staff, and I served as interpreters. Many deals were actually finalized during the ten-odd minutes spent waiting for the food to be served," Shalabi said. The restaurant became a landmark in the community of foreign merchants in Yiwu, underpinned by the city's supportive and convenient business environment. Administrative services for foreigners, such as the consultation, appointment booking, and online processing of accommodation registration, visas, and work permits, were quick and smooth. In the business sector, the local government launched online platforms for matters including foreign investment and the opening of personal foreign exchange settlement accounts. Foreign merchants could also look up various public services through smart digital tools and personalized guides. "No matter how big or small an issue, a single phone call could sort it out. This is the 'Yiwu speed,'" Shalabi said. With local government support, Shalabi established "Nad's Home," a volunteer organization dedicated to helping foreigners in Yiwu solve problems. It also organizes various volunteer activities on a regular basis. On June 5, 2014, Chinese President Xi Jinping delivered an important speech at the opening ceremony of the Sixth Ministerial Conference of China-Arab States Cooperation Forum. In the speech, he spoke about the story of Shalabi who put down roots in China and realized his life dreams. Following that, people came from far and wide in admiration. As the original facilities and space could no longer keep pace with the growing number of patrons, Shalabi leased a nearby three-story venue spanning over 1,000 square meters, renaming the establishment "Beyti." "'Beyti' means 'my home' in Arabic. I want everyone who comes here to feel like they are returning home," said Shalabi. The most eye-catching feature of the new restaurant is a prominent display wall featuring high-quality Belt and Road cooperation. Embossed on the wall is a relief map of the Yixin'ou (Yiwu-Xinjiang-Europe) China-Europe freight railway route starting from Yiwu, with countries along the way marked. "Many foreign merchants didn't know about high-quality Belt and Road cooperation or the China-Europe freight trains at first. After seeing the wall, they realized trains leave Yiwu with Chinese goods for Europe, connecting our hometowns with Yiwu and making us feel that we are one big family. The freight train service is more than a trade route. It is a dialogue between civilizations on mutual benefit and win-win cooperation," Shalabi said. The convenience of trade and commerce has brought tangible benefits to Shalabi. "Today, 99 percent of the ingredients for the restaurant can be purchased locally, and a single phone call brings them right to our doorstep," he said. "My story is much more than just an entrepreneurial journey. It is a story of exchange and mutual learning among civilizations," Shalabi said. "I want to tell that young Jordanian stepping off the train over 20 years ago: Don't worry, you will find your career direction here, and you will find a true sense of belonging," he added. item.title: Tennis gains fresh momentum in China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Tennis gains fresh momentum in China Spectators pack the stands at the 2026 China Open in Beijing. (Photo from the official website of the China Open) As the Guangzhou Open drew to a close, the China tennis season entered its final stretch. Now in its second year as a branded series, the season included eight international professional tournaments at different levels across multiple cities, creating a tennis festival that lasted nearly two months. Breakthrough performances by Chinese players, closer integration of sports, culture, tourism, and commerce, and greater global exposure for China's stories all contributed to the season's outstanding performance. Throughout the season, Chinese players competed across the country, delivering one surprise after another. China's Zheng Qinwen captured the women's singles title at the 2026 China Open, becoming the first Chinese woman to win the title in the tournament's 20-year history. After undergoing elbow surgery and seeing her world ranking plunge, Zheng faced down outside criticism and fought her way back. "I am just so grateful that I found the inner fire back. Right now, I'm trying to reach the best version of myself," she said. Her journey from a difficult period of injury recovery to winning her maiden WTA 1000 crown on home soil is a testament to her resilience. Zheng Qinwen competes at the China Open in Beijing. (Photo from the official website of the China Open) Beyond the excitement on court, tournaments in the China tennis season have become important driving forces of consumption and economic growth, while tennis is becoming a popular lifestyle choice. The China Open set new records for both attendance and consumer spending. More than 450,000 spectator visits were recorded during the tournament, with spectators from outside Beijing accounting for 60 percent. Ticket revenue reached 132 million yuan (about $19.78 million), while related consumer spending surpassed 55 million yuan, both hitting record highs. Sales of licensed merchandise doubled from a year earlier. The influx of spectators gave a boost to consumer spending across the city. The Shanghai Masters extended the tournament experience beyond the courts, creating diverse settings and opportunities for people to experience tennis in different parts of the city. This year, it launched a carnival featuring open training sessions, a tennis-themed museum, and celebrity exhibition matches beyond regular match hours. "The tournament is no longer confined to a single venue. Through innovative activities such as a citywide stamp collecting activity, and combined tickets for multiple tournaments, we are bringing the excitement of tennis into neighborhoods across the city, extending the value of the tournament brand, and unlocking the potential for high-end consumption," said Yang Yibin, chairman of Shanghai Juss Sports and Entertainment Group. This year's tournament attracted nearly 250,000 spectator visits, around 12 percent of whom came from overseas. Total revenue reached approximately 500 million yuan, with sponsorship, ticket sales, and revenue from TV broadcasting rights sharing all hitting record highs. The Wuhan Open in Wuhan, central China's Hubei province, teamed up with shopping areas and scenic areas to offer exclusive discounts to ticket holders, connecting the tournament with tourism resources across the province. It attracted a record 202,700 spectator visits, hitting a new high. The tournament generated an estimated 890 million yuan in overall economic benefits, up 26.24 percent from the previous year. The Chengdu Open ran dedicated shuttle buses between the tournament venue and shopping areas around the city. On board, spectators could find shopping guides and scan QR codes to access ticket-holder offers. By showing their match tickets, they could enjoy discounts and special offers on dining, shopping, culture and tourism experience at nearly 3,000 businesses across the city. Tennis enjoys global appeal, and the China tennis season provides a platform for exchange. Beyond the courts, international players can experience Chinese culture firsthand and share their stories of China with audiences around the world. Elena Rybakina, the world No. 1 in women's singles, experiences Chinese culture at the Yuebo Academy by Dongqian Lake in Ningbo, east China's Zhejiang province. (Photo courtesy of the Dongqian Lake scenic area) During the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, the Hangzhou Open organized a nighttime cruise on West Lake aboard the "Moon Boat," offering players a close-up experience of traditional Chinese music, classical dance and the romantic charm of worshipping the moon. Ahead of the Ningbo Open, Elena Rybakina, the world No. 1 in women's singles, visited the Yuebo Academy by Dongqian Lake. Dressed in Song Dynasty (960-1279) attire, she tried her hand at traditional tea making and painting oil-paper umbrellas. Spanish player Alejandro Davidovich Fokina visited a Shu brocade cultural and creative park in Chengdu, where he watched the intricate process of weaving the traditional fabric on a drawloom. He said: "Tennis is all about rhythm and patience, while every inch of this brocade reflects a dedication passed down through generations." On and off the court, more and more foreign players, referees and technical officials have learned to exchange greetings in Chinese. Chinese spectators, meanwhile, have won widespread praise from players for their spectator etiquette. What has made an especially deep impression are the thoughtful gifts from Chinese fans, including hand-drawn portraits of tennis stars, handwritten letters of support and city-themed souvenirs. After winning the China Open, Serbian tennis star Novak Djokovic said: "Chinese fans are among the best in the world. They bring me all kinds of gifts and wait for me for so long. Their thoughtfulness is truly touching." Bai Xilin, director of the Tennis Administration Center of China's General Administration of Sport, said the China tennis season demonstrates the sport's value on multiple fronts. "More and more people are coming to tennis tournaments not just for the matches, but also to experience the culture and emotional connections they offer," he said. item.title: SE China's Fujian steps up efforts to strengthen its role as core area of 21st Century Maritime Silk Road
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
SE China's Fujian steps up efforts to strengthen its role as core area of 21st Century Maritime Silk Road A cargo ship is berthed at the Yuanhai Container Terminal in Xiamen, southeast China's Fujian province, as cargo handling operations are underway. (Photo/Zeng Demeng) Thriving on the sea, southeast China's Fujian province has made notable progress in expanding marine cooperation and strengthening international exchanges. The World Maritime Equipment Conference 2026, held in Fuzhou, the provincial capital, brought together 175 guests from 43 Belt and Road partner countries to explore industrial collaboration in the marine economy. Juncao technology, developed in Fujian, has been introduced to more than 100 countries and regions, with demonstration bases established in 24 countries. In the first three quarters of this year, Fujian's imports and exports with Belt and Road partner countries reached 816.33 billion yuan ($122.38 billion), up 9 percent year on year, marking a record high for the same period. In recent years, the province has continued to improve its integrated transport network spanning sea, land, and air, intensify economic, trade, and investment cooperation, and expand people-to-people and cultural exchanges, striving to strengthen its role as a core area of the 21st Century Maritime Silk Road by facilitating global connectivity, promoting win-win cooperation, and fostering closer ties among peoples. Accelerated infrastructure construction has helped forge closer economic and trade ties for Fujian. Business representatives discuss cooperation on marine equipment at the fourth Fujian International Marine Equipment Expo in Fuzhou, southeast China's Fujian province, Oct. 17, 2026. (Photo/Xie Guiming) On November 7, the cargo ship Xin Xu Zhou, loaded with Chinese-made goods, slowly departed from the Haitian Terminal of Xiamen Port in Xiamen, Fujian, heading for Southeast Asia along a shipping route of the Silk Road Maritime, China's first comprehensive international logistics service brand and platform centered on maritime shipping under the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI). "Since its inauguration eight years ago, the Silk Road Maritime shipping network has expanded to 160 routes, connecting 153 ports in 50 countries and regions, while its alliance has grown to 393 members," said Li Nan, general manager of Fujian Silk Road Maritime Operation Co. Ltd, the operator of the Silk Road Maritime brand. On land, China-Europe (Central Asia) freight trains operating from Fujian now reach more than 30 cities in 13 countries, serving as a vital transport link connecting inland regions with the sea. In the air, the province is steadily advancing its air connectivity project under the BRI. The airports in Fuzhou and Xiamen, the province's two major gateway hubs, both serve as regional aviation hubs, forming an extensive network of international air links. With access to China's vast central and western hinterland, and situated between Yangtze River Delta to the north and Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area to the south, Fujian is leveraging its strategic position as a transport corridor to continuously strengthen economic, trade, and investment cooperation and deepen industrial and supply chain connections. These efforts are translating into tangible benefits for all partners. By promoting exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations, Fujian has continuously expanded its international "circle of friends." Participants in a Juncao technology training session for developing countries held at Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University display their Juncao "creations." (Photo courtesy of Fujian Daily) On October 17, representatives from 24 countries gathered in Fuzhou for the 21st Century Maritime Silk Road Local Government Cooperation and International Friendship Cities Dialogue. Discussions covered topics including global governance and the marine economy, resulting in seven cooperation documents. The participants also visited landmarks including Sanfangqixiang, or the Three Lanes and Seven Alleys, a historic and cultural block in Fuzhou, to experience the city's unique charm, reflected in its openness and inclusiveness in the new era and the harmonious coexistence of its historical heritage and modern life. "Fuzhou has a rich history and its people are friendly and kind. I would strongly recommend that more people visit the city," said Saullo Branco, Asian markets director at Investe Piauí, Brazil . To date, Fujian has established sister-province, state, city and district relationships with 138 local governments in 53 countries. Cultural exchanges have played an important role in expanding the province's international network of friendships. Fujian has strengthened international cooperation to boost people's livelihood, fostering bonds of friendship that resonate deeply with the peoples of many countries. On October 16, 22 participants from four countries, including Central African Republic, visited China National Engineering Research Center of Juncao Technology at Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University to receive systematic training in the cultivation of Juncao, a hybrid grass originally developed in China for mushroom cultivation, and mushroom production. The university has organized more than 480 international training sessions at home and abroad, attracting approximately 23,000 participants from 118 countries. At the college of information and electronic engineering of Liming Vocational University, located in Quanzhou, Fujian, a Malaysian student was seen dismantling a car alongside an instructor. "Here, I have the opportunity to learn about many advanced new energy vehicles. The combination of theoretical instruction and hands-on training has been extremely beneficial to me," the student said. Fujian has also sent 21 medical assistance teams to Senegal and 18 to Botswana, providing medical services to more than 6.9 million patients and performing over 200,000 surgeries. Meanwhile, the province continues to expand high-standard opening-up in international education cooperation and develop its "Study in Fujian" brand. By carrying out a range of "small and beautiful" livelihood projects, Fujian is helping deliver tangible benefits and improve the lives of people in Belt and Road partner countries. item.title: Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-13
Xi to attend APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, related events in Shenzhen BEIJING, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will chair the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting and deliver remarks, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced Friday. The meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19 under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," the spokesperson said. The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 18 under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the spokesperson said, adding that President Xi will attend the opening ceremony and deliver a keynote speech. President Xi will hold a welcome banquet for participating leaders and representatives, and hold bilateral meetings with foreign leaders on the sidelines of the meeting, the spokesperson added.
